title: Context-economy baseline over real orchestrator runs (IMP-0018 Phase 0)
summary: `orchestrate context-economy` run read-only over the local orchestrator home on 2026-10-02 (report: docs/orchestrator-os/self-audit/context-economy-baseline.json; aggregates only, privacy check passed over 1388 strings). 20 runs, 666 worker/planner calls, 653 with exact provider-reported usage (13 unavailable, 0 estimated or synthetic). Amplification = input tokens / estimated prompt tokens (characters/4): pooled 104.8x across all calls (median 53.2, p90 645.4); median/p90 per role: implementer 141.2/980.6, repairer 189.0/851.1, test_author 164.4/712.3, planner 81.9/327.9, reviewer 11.7/43.6. Median cache-read share 0.84, so most input is cached re-read rather than fresh tokens. Output is ~1.6% of input pooled. Long-session growth: per-node last/first input ratio median 0.78 (nodes with 2-3 calls) and 0.43 (4+ calls), i.e. later calls in a session are not larger than the first; per-run cumulative-input growth exponent is >1 in most runs (range 0.58-1.88), meaning cumulative input grows superlinearly with call count. Fan-out: 527 worker nodes; worker input 255.8M tokens vs planner 7.8M; duplicated fixed overhead 253.4M tokens (share 0.9905 of worker input); retry/repeat-attempt input 47.7M (26 retries, 63 escalations, 15 fallbacks). Checkpoint-resume: across the 10 runs with resumes, resume overhead is 26.4M of 153.9M run input (share 0.1715; resume-first-call share 0.1504). Caveats: amplification denominators are character estimates, the fan-out overhead share is a model-based upper bound (worker input minus a per-worker minimal-prompt estimate), and negative overhead appeared in 5 calls.
